We learn a lot in one semester, so especially the Japanese language is very hard, we don't enough time to process all of the topics completely. For example, reading hiragana for the final exam and listening exam for the midterm was hard because we are learning Japanese for the first time in our lives, so time limits were not enough some time and difficulty levels were a little bit high for the Japanese beginning level in exams.
İlk başta Japonca öğrenmenin çok zor olacağını düşünsem de, beklediğimden daha anlaşılır ve kolay geldi. Bence başlangıç seviyesindeki bir ders için konular yeterli.

It is not difficult at all as long as you study(preparing flashcards from the beginning and using them is a good idea). We learn hiragana but not katakana, so that makes things easier. Plus, the textbook we used had the romaji equivalent of the text until around week 9, so students are not expected to learn it well enough to be able to read texts written in it immediately. In addition, self-study material is provided for those who want to learn more than they are required to. For example, when we were taught the Japanese word for around 5 different occupations, there was a list on moodle with around 20 or so extra words that we could further study if we wanted to. We also were not required to learn how to write kanji but there were worksheets for that. Overall, the course is not difficult to follow and further self-study is encouraged.

course:

course: Japanese itself has its own challenges, particularly its alphabets, but taking this course from a native Japanese teacher is a huge advantage and contributes positively to the learning process.

One of the strongest aspects of the course is that Japanese is a very enjoyable language to learn. Thanks to the textbook we used, we focused on daily conversation, which allowed us to make progress quickly. The course was not heavily grammar-based; instead, it emphasized speaking, which made it easier to follow and more engaging.
The challenging part, of course, is that Japanese uses a different writing system, so it takes some time to get used to it. However, it is not something to be afraid of.
The textbooks are great for the A1 level with necessary and relevant content.
